lesson_title: The Day the Cod Ran Out
hook_text: Sailors once said you could catch cod off Canada by lowering a basket into the sea, and then, in 1992, they were gone.
clip_script: For five hundred years, the seas off Newfoundland were packed with cod. Then came factory ships, sonar and nets the size of football fields. Catches broke records. Scientists warned. Nobody listened. In 1992, the cod had almost vanished. Canada banned cod fishing, and tens of thousands of people lost their jobs. Thirty years later, the cod still haven't fully returned. Today, more than a third of the world's fish stocks are over-fished. South Africa knows this story too. West Coast crayfish are scarce. Perlemoen was poached so heavily that the fishery closed in 2008. And as sardines run short, African penguins go hungry. Fish are a renewable resource, but only if we leave enough of them in the sea to breed.
visual_style: Old paintings of cod-filled seas; a giant factory trawler hauling a bulging net; a sonar screen full of fish; empty harbour boats in Newfoundland; a crayfish on a rock; confiscated bags of abalone; an African penguin on a Cape beach.
pacing: Abundance at first, rising tension, a sudden stop at the collapse.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn why over-fishing happens and what it does to people and the oceans.
